title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Maritime Courts May Apply the Small Claims Procedure

articles.content_en:
June 19, 2013
Supreme People's Court
Reply on Whether Maritime Courts May Apply the Small Claims Procedure
Interpretation No. 16 [2013] of the Supreme People's Court
Shanghai Higher People's Court:
Your Request for Instructions on the Application of the Small Claims Procedure by Maritime Courts (Shanghai Higher People's Court Document No. 5 [2013]) has been received. Upon study, the reply is as follows:
The Small Claims Procedure is provided for in the chapter on Summary Procedure of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China revised in 2012, and Article 98 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a maritime court may apply the summary procedure. Therefore, a maritime court may apply the small claims procedure to hear simple maritime and marine trade cases.
The amount in controversy for applying the small claims procedure shall be limited to 30 percent of the average annual wage of employed persons in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the maritime court accepting the case or its dispatched tribunal is located in the preceding year.
